record.original_question: Fix an ample line bundle H on a minimal surface X with kappa(X)>0, and move H closer to the canonical class KX as in Theorem 3.2 to obtain a moduli-theoretic sequence of flips giving an analogy of the minimal model program for M(H), the moduli scheme of H-stable sheaves. What geometric improvement of M(H) can be proved along this flip sequence, especially in cases where M(H) has only log-terminal singularities so that the birational maps define a genuine minimal model program, and what can be learned by instead starting with H near KX and gradually moving H away from KX while observing the wall-crossing flips?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3. We pick an ample line bundle H on X and move it closer to KX , then we obtain an analogy of MMP of M (H) by Theorem 3.2. (1) Can we investigate how M (H) is improved by this moduli-theoretic sequence of flips? Especially, the case where M (H) admits only log-terminal singularities is more desirable, because the above-mentioned birational maps give the genuine MMP in this case. Also it is more desirable that the structure of the starting point M (H) is easy to understand.
(2) It can be interesting if one starts H near KX and gradually moves H away from KX , and one observes flips occuring from wall-crossing as in Theorem 3.2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex minimal projective surface with Kodaira dimension $\kappa(X) > 0$ and canonical line bundle $K_X$. Fix Chern data (rank and Chern classes) for torsion-free coherent sheaves on $X$, and for each ample line bundle $H$ on $X$ let $M(H)$ denote the moduli scheme of Gieseker $H$-semistable sheaves with that Chern data. Assume the following framework: as $H$ varies in the ample cone, $M(H)$ undergoes wall-crossings which, when $H$ is moved toward $K_X$, produce a sequence of birational maps that behave like flips with respect to the canonical class, providing a moduli-theoretic analogue of the minimal model program for $M(H)$.

(1) Starting from a general ample $H$ and moving $H$ toward $K_X$, describe precisely how the geometry of $M(H)$ improves along the resulting sequence of moduli-theoretic flips. In particular, in the situation where $M(H)$ has only log-terminal singularities — so that the birational maps constitute a genuine minimal model program in the sense of Mori theory — determine the resulting minimal (or canonical) model and describe its geometry, ideally choosing the starting $H$ so that the initial moduli space $M(H)$ has an explicit, easy-to-understand structure.

(2) Conversely, starting with $H$ near $K_X$ and moving $H$ gradually away from $K_X$, describe the wall-crossing flips that occur and what geometric information about the family $\{M(H)\}_H$ they reveal.
artifact.category_tag: Moduli of stable sheaves and MMP via wall-crossing
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction. Related results exist for K3 surfaces (Bayer–Macrì, MMP for moduli of sheaves on K3s via wall-crossing) and for some elliptic surfaces (arXiv:1908.05027), but no general resolution for arbitrary minimal surfaces with positive Kodaira dimension appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: MMP for Moduli of Sheaves on K3s via Wall-Crossing
status_evidence.snippet: Wall-crossing with respect to Bridgeland stability conditions systematically describes the birational geometry of moduli of stable sheaves on K3 surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous MMP-via-wall-crossing is established for K3 surfaces, but not for general minimal surfaces of positive Kodaira dimension.

status_evidence.title: The Kodaira dimension and singularities of moduli of stable sheaves on some elliptic surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Kodaira dimension and singularities of moduli of stable sheaves on certain elliptic surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for elliptic surfaces, indicating the general problem remains open.
